Methods for zinbreg objects

Source: R/methods-zinbreg.R
zinbreg-methods.Rd

Standard accessor, summary, and prediction methods for fits from zinbreg().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
coef(object, model = c("full", "count", "zero"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
vcov(object, model = c("full", "count", "zero"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
residuals(object, type = c("response", "pearson"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
predict(object, newdata, type = c("response", "count", "zero"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'zinbreg'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.zinbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

Arguments

object, x

An object of class "zinbreg" (or "summary.zinbreg").

model

For coef() and vcov(): "full" (count and zero coefficients, named count_* and zero_* as in pscl::zeroinfl()), "count", or "zero". \(\log\theta\) is not included (as in zeroinfl()); its standard error is in object$SE.logtheta.

...

Further arguments (ignored or passed on to stats::printCoefmat()).

type

For residuals(): "response" (\(y_i - \hat E(Y_i)\)) or "pearson" (response residual divided by \(\sqrt{\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(Y_i)}\)). For predict(): "response" (\((1-\hat\pi)\hat\mu\), the mean of \(Y\)), "count" (\(\hat\mu\), the mean of the NB component), or "zero" (\(\hat\pi\), the probability of a structural zero).

newdata

Optional data frame for prediction.

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

Value

coef(), vcov(): estimates and covariance matrix. logLik(): a "logLik" object with df = p + q + 1, so AIC()/BIC() work. fitted(): \((1-\hat\pi_i)\hat\mu_i\). residuals(), predict(): see type. nobs(): number of observations. summary(): object of class "summary.zinbreg" with count and zero coefficient tables.

Examples

set.seed(3)
n <- 500
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(n), z = rnorm(n))
d$y <- ifelse(rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-1 + d$z)) == 1, 0,
              rnbinom(n, size = 1.5, mu = exp(1 + 0.5 * d$x)))
fit <- zinbreg(y ~ x | z, data = d)
summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> zinbreg(formula = y ~ x | z, data = d)
#> 
#> Pearson residuals:
#>     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
#> -1.1146 -0.6764 -0.3953  0.3179  6.0266 
#> 
#> Count model coefficients (NB2 with log link):
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)  1.10088    0.06628  16.608  < 2e-16 ***
#> x            0.51751    0.05361   9.652  < 2e-16 ***
#> Log(theta)   0.65011    0.18921   3.436 0.000591 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#> 
#> Zero-inflation model coefficients (binomial with logit link):
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)  -0.9439     0.2215  -4.260 2.04e-05 ***
#> z             1.2761     0.2235   5.709 1.14e-08 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#> 
#> Theta: 1.916  (SE 0.3625 )
#> Log-likelihood: -927.701 on 5 Df;  AIC: 1865.4   BIC: 1886.47 
#> Number of observations: 500   EM iterations: 37 
AIC(fit)
#> [1] 1865.402
predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(x = 0, z = c(-1, 0, 1)), type = "zero")
#>         1         2         3 
#> 0.0979755 0.2801227 0.5822989
